title: CPTS arsenal
intro: A practical, command-first reference for the CPTS path, organised by what you are attacking: the network, a web app, an Active Directory domain, a Windows or Linux host, credentials, and the access and pivoting that tie them together. Pick a target to see the tools that matter there, or search by port, service or tool. Every entry is a working reference, not an exploit kit: use it only against systems you are authorised to test.

stages.name: Network & services
stages.blurb: What is on the wire: discover hosts and ports, fingerprint the services, and attack the network-facing ones, SMB, SNMP, databases and remote logins. The first move on almost every box.
checklist: Full TCP and top-UDP scan complete
Every open port's service and version identified
Default and weak credentials tried where safe

stages.name: Web
stages.blurb: The web attack surface: fingerprint the stack, discover content and vhosts, and exploit the app itself, injection, upload, LFI, SSRF and the known-app CVEs.
checklist: Inputs tested for injection (SQLi, command, SSTI)
Known CVEs matched to the app version

stages.name: Active Directory
stages.blurb: Attacking a Windows domain: enumerate users, groups and trusts, map attack paths with BloodHound, then roast, relay, delegate and dump your way towards Domain Admin.
checklist: Domain, DC and naming convention identified
A path to Domain Admin mapped

stages.name: Windows host
stages.blurb: Owning a single Windows box: enumerate the host and your token, escalate to SYSTEM, and dump the local credential stores. The interactive Windows and credential-access maps go deeper.
checklist: Token privileges and integrity level checked

stages.name: Linux host
stages.blurb: Owning a single Linux box: enumerate the host, walk the privesc primitives, SUID/SGID, sudo, capabilities, cron and PATH, and get to root. The interactive Linux map goes deeper.

stages.name: Credentials & cracking
stages.blurb: Everything to do with secrets: hunt for them on hosts and shares, build wordlists tuned to the target, and crack the hashes you capture offline with John and Hashcat.
checklist: Hosts and shares hunted for stored credentials
Cracked credentials fed back into access

stages.name: Access, transfers & pivoting
stages.blurb: The plumbing of an engagement: catch and stabilise shells, move files on and off a host, generate payloads, and tunnel through a foothold to reach the next network.
checklist: Shell caught and upgraded to a full TTY
File transfer works in both directions
Payload matched to target OS and architecture
Internal network reached through a pivot
